intro: Bologna rewards visitors with medieval porticoes, lively piazzas and some of Italy's best food. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro yet; a tram network is under construction.
TPER buses cover the city; single ticket €2.30, valid 75 min, €2.50 on board.
Day pass costs about €9; buy tickets at tabacchi or newsstands.
Taxis are metered; ride apps like Uber are limited, local apps work better.
Driving in the centre is restricted; cars are banned in parts during the day.
Walking is easy and pleasant; bike hire is cheap, about €1-2 per 15 min.

piazza_maggiore.name: Piazza Maggiore
piazza_maggiore.tip: Sit on the steps of San Petronio in the evening when locals gather. Look for the bricked-up window on the Palazzo del Podestà.

two_towers.name: Two Towers (Due Torri)
two_towers.price_text: Around EUR 5 to climb the Asinelli tower; check on the day
two_towers.hours: Climb usually daytime; check on the day
two_towers.tip: Climb the taller Asinelli tower for the best view. The Garisenda leans more and cannot be entered.

archiginnasio.name: Archiginnasio of Bologna
archiginnasio.price_text: Small entry fee for the Anatomical Theatre; check on the day
archiginnasio.hours: Usually morning to afternoon; closed some days, check on the day
archiginnasio.tip: The wooden Anatomical Theatre is the highlight. Go early to avoid groups.

university.name: University of Bologna
university.tip: It claims to be the oldest university in the world. Wander the streets around Via Zamboni to feel student life.

quadrilatero.name: Quadrilatero food streets
quadrilatero.price_text: Free to walk; food paid per item
quadrilatero.hours: Market stalls mostly morning to early afternoon; shops vary
quadrilatero.tip: Narrow lanes east of Piazza Maggiore full of delis and market stalls. Go before lunch for the freshest food.

mercato_erbe.name: Mercato delle Erbe
mercato_erbe.price_text: Free to enter; food paid per item
mercato_erbe.hours: Market daytime; food counters into the evening; check on the day
mercato_erbe.tip: Covered market with produce by day and casual eating and drinks later. Good for a cheap lunch.

san_luca.name: Sanctuary of San Luca and portico walk
san_luca.price_text: Free to walk; small charge for some transport
san_luca.tip: Walk up under the long portico for a city view. It is a steady climb, so wear comfortable shoes.

santo_stefano.name: Santo Stefano complex
santo_stefano.tip: A cluster of old churches with a quiet courtyard. A calm break from the busy centre.

food_tour.name: Bologna food walking tour
food_tour.price_text: Roughly EUR 50–80 per person; check on the day
food_tour.tip: A guided walk through the food streets with tastings. Book ahead and say if you have dietary needs.

portico_walk.name: Porticoes of Bologna walk
portico_walk.tip: Bologna's covered walkways are a UNESCO site. Walk them in the rain or heat for shade and shelter.

via_zamboni.name: Via Zamboni student quarter walk
via_zamboni.tip: The main street of the university area, busy with students and cheap bars. Livelier in the evening.

mambo.name: MAMbo Museum of Modern Art
mambo.price_text: Around EUR 6; check on the day
mambo.hours: Closed Monday; daytime other days, check on the day
mambo.tip: Modern art in a former bakery. A good rainy-day option outside the busiest streets.

pinacoteca.name: Pinacoteca Nazionale
pinacoteca.price_text: Around EUR 6; check on the day
pinacoteca.hours: Closed Monday; daytime other days, check on the day
pinacoteca.tip: Paintings from the region's past. Quiet and rarely crowded.

giardini_margherita.name: Giardini Margherita
giardini_margherita.tip: The city's main park, good for a rest and a picnic. Popular with students on sunny days.

aperitivo.name: Aperitivo in the centre
aperitivo.price_text: Roughly EUR 6–12 per drink; check on the day
aperitivo.tip: Order a drink in the early evening and snacks often come with it. Prices and rules vary by bar.

bologna_centrale.name: Bologna Centrale station area
bologna_centrale.tip: The main rail hub for day trips to Florence, Modena and Ravenna. Keep an eye on bags in the busy hall.

san_petronio.name: Basilica of San Petronio
san_petronio.price_text: Free entry; small charge for some areas, check on the day
san_petronio.tip: The unfinished facade faces Piazza Maggiore. Step inside to see the huge sundial line on the floor.

tortellini_class.name: Pasta-making class
tortellini_class.price_text: Roughly EUR 50–100 per person; check on the day
tortellini_class.tip: Learn to fold tortellini with a local cook. Book ahead and confirm the language of the class.

via_indipendenza.name: Via dell'Indipendenza walk
via_indipendenza.tip: The main shopping street linking the station to the centre. Handy route on foot from the train.

piazza_santo_stefano_market.name: Piazza Santo Stefano evening scene
piazza_santo_stefano_market.price_text: Free to walk; drinks paid separately
piazza_santo_stefano_market.tip: A triangular square where people gather for drinks on warm nights. Good for a relaxed evening.

stays.why: Walk to Piazza Maggiore, the porticoes and most trattorias. Best for first-timers.
Next to the station for day trips to Florence or Modena; 15 minutes on foot to the centre.
Lively bars and cheap eats around Via Zamboni; good budget base, can be noisy at night.
Quieter residential area near the station and Porta Saragozza; good value, still walkable.

food: Order tagliatelle al ragù, not spaghetti bolognese; locals eat tortellini in brodo too.
Try a plate of mortadella and crescentine (fried dough) at a casual osteria.
The Quadrilatero market streets near Piazza Maggiore are good for a cheap grazing lunch.
Book dinner ahead on weekends; popular trattorias fill up fast.
Aperitivo around 18:00–19:00 often comes with snacks; check the price before ordering.
more_time: Day trip to Modena by train for balsamic and the food market; check times on the day.
Swap a museum morning for a walk up to San Luca under the long portico; check opening hours.
Take a train to Ferrara or Parma for a half-day of Renaissance streets and food.
